analysis:
Examined all supplied BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (lines 1–1178) and the complete patch adding HEAD lines 484–497. The change introduces add-on hold bookkeeping, a drain task and generation, lease monitoring, a local IPC server, paths, and authentication/clock/timeout seams. Stored state alone does not establish an authorization bypass, data disclosure, or availability regression; no supported finding is identified in this scope.
Existing surrounding contracts include encrypted chunk/terminal ordering (BASE 55–85; T-008), per-process X25519 generation (895; A-003/T-011), cancellation tracking (587–598; T-010), model identity/cache eligibility (994–996, 1055–1056; T-012/T-027/T-041), and reconnect/admission barriers (447–455; T-053). These excerpts contain no changed implementations of those controls.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+AddonHold and AddonIPCServer together with their startup, admission, unload, renewal, and shutdown callers: verify who can acquire/renew/release a hold, socket ownership and peer authentication across TB-003, bounded leases and drain failure handling under TB-007, stale-task generation protection, and whether holds affect authorization or reconnection under TB-002/TB-011. Confirm production cannot select the authentication override inadvertently. These are unverified new IPC/lifecycle contracts, not observed missing controls. Only selected threat definitions were supplied verbatim; unchanged callers and the new implementations are outside this batch.
